What you already have¹
If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes:
MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement.
MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs.
CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability.
/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--f640816d-5ebe-48f5-8d58-7759c26d005d/what-you-may-consider--2-.jpg?quality=85&preferwebp=true
What you may consider²

You might have insurance protection policies, but are you truly covered for health issues and increased risk of accidents that come with age? The key is ensuring you have enough coverage to avoid dipping into your retirement savings.
You’ll need:
Critical Illness Plan
Integrated Shield Plan

Be protected from the financial impact of serious conditions such as cancer, stroke, and heart attack, so you can recover with peace of mind and continue supporting your family in the event of a critical illness.

Wealth
Your golden years are the time to kick back and live the life you desire. In addition to securing your protection, planning for your goals, including legacy planning, is essential.
https://s7ap1.scene7.com/is/image/prudentialholdingsstage/what_you_should_have-4?qlt=85&wid=320&ts=1772446002857&$FullWidth$&dpr=off
Basics – what you should have
A Plan For Monthly Payouts³ Choose from three CPF LIFE plans to fit your needs.
Emergency Funds⁴,⁵ At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses for rainy days.
Legacy Planning⁴,⁵ A plan for a will, family trusts, life insurance, powers of attorney, and CPF nominations.
Invest At Least 10% Of Take-Home Pay⁵ For retirement, if you are currently earning a steady income and not yet retired.
https://s7ap1.scene7.com/is/image/prudentialholdingsstage/what_you_may_consider-8?qlt=85&wid=320&ts=1772445885392&$FullWidth$&dpr=off
What you may consider

It pays to start planning for retirement early. To see if your nest egg is sufficient, consider the kind of lifestyle you want to lead, how long you expect to be in retirement, and what amount of income you desire.
Here's how to find out if your savings will last⁶:
Calculate Needs: Review your expenses before and during retirement.
Assess Resources: Add your savings and any monthly payouts.
Consider Inflation: Take into account inflation and your expected investment returns.
Find The Gap: Subtract the needs from the resources.
If the result is negative, you may find it challenging to maintain a comfortable retirement.
More ways to bridge the gap⁴,⁵:
Investment Or Savings Plans
Tap Into Your Assets If you are 55 years old or above, explore monetising your property (Silver Housing Bonus, Lease Buyback Scheme, renting out room / flat).
Spend Within Your Means
